beats.say: This old build portal stopped at the parser test. You need the traceback for a local incident draft. Where would you put the cursor?
Open Failed tests. The panel shows parser dot py, line eighteen. The missing field is status. The same browser session also shows a deploy control.

The traceback is painted on a canvas. A typed tool could limit a request to one run, but this old portal has no supported API or reliable selector for the failure line. A GUI agent can propose a click on either control. The host still decides which action may run.
Rewind to the first decision. Before the host opens this browser, look at the requested session. A reused profile, the mail site, and a deploy capability. Should it launch?

Reject that request. Start with a fresh profile inside an isolated worker. Allow only the CI site through the network boundary and give the session read-only credentials. Limit storage, steps and time. A fresh profile alone would still inherit the powers of its account.

The host brokers the login. The model sees the run number and the resulting page. Passwords, home cookies and the host clipboard stay outside. Restrict uploads and downloads too. Even an allowed page can receive data typed into it.

The model proposes opening the matching run. The host checks that the action fits the task, target, and current state before dispatch. It opens the run. The search field already contains the run number. Once the run-detail heading shows RUN-78432, the host captures a fresh observation. Each input gets this check.

A browser driver can do that in a headless browser. A native app would need a display and a focused window of its own. Pin the adapter to its input units and result format. The loop ends at verified completion, a deadline, a step limit, or a safety boundary.

title: One target in five coordinate spaces

beats.say: A model's point belongs to the image it observed. Look at the cross on the tab. It is one hundred thirty-two pixels right and sixty-six down from the padded image corner. Which corner starts the actual crop?
Start at the inner corner. Remove the thirty-two pixels of left padding and sixteen at the top. Relative to that corner the cross is at one hundred, fifty.

Restore the crop's original scale. The crop was shrunk from six hundred forty by four hundred to three hundred twenty by two hundred. Multiply each displacement by two. Then add the crop origin to place the cross at three hundred, one hundred fifty in the native screenshot.

This screenshot covers the viewport and uses two device pixels per CSS pixel on each axis. Divide by two. Send one hundred fifty, seventy-five to a browser driver that expects viewport CSS pixels. A CSS-scale capture already uses those units. Desktop chrome or full-page scrolling changes the origin too.
Try the same rule on an uncropped image. Six hundred by four hundred becomes fifteen hundred by a thousand. Where does the marked point land in native pixels?

Scale each axis by two and a half. One hundred eighty becomes four hundred fifty. One hundred twenty becomes three hundred. Now look at mark seven on the tab. The model can name the mark. The host looks up its box in the map for this tab and frame. A new layout needs a fresh map.

title: When the list moves under the pointer

beats.say: Frame two shows Failed tests in the second row. The gold tip is a proposed click. Keep your finger on that spot.
A new row slides in as the run loads more artifacts. If the host sent that old click now, which panel would open?
Artifacts. The host compares the proposal's session and frame with the live view. Frame two has expired. Discard the proposal. The run overview stays open, and the failure click count is still zero.
Capture frame three. The accessibility tree gives a role and a name. Two runs have a tab named Failed tests. Scope the search to this run. If two matches remain, observe again or ask a human.

There is one match in this run. Its row has settled, it is enabled and nothing covers it. Move the proposed point to that row. Now click. The new view shows the parser traceback. A role can name the tab while pixels supply the line painted inside it.
The host saves a local draft for the intended incident. Check its run number, failure line and artifact reference against the open panel. They match. The read-only inspection ends here.

title: One click, two views of the result

beats.say: In a separate, authorized note-writing exercise, the reviewer has approved this exact note. Watch the incident form while the host clicks Submit once. A click proves that the host sent an input event.
The screen still looks exactly the same. The server has a pending request. From that screen alone, should the host click again?
Wait. The server processes the request and stores one note. The form still shows zero. A second submission could create a second note. The host needs evidence from the record that owns the change.
Read the incident record. The receipt links this request to the accepted note on the intended incident, and the content matches. The host can verify this submission and stop after one click.

Suppose the bounded read had timed out instead. The dispatch would still be in the log. Its outcome would be unknown to the host. Record that uncertainty and escalate. Reserve never sent for a proposal stopped before dispatch.
Back in the inspection, reading the failed step is within this task. Preparing a local note is also allowed when the note stays on the host. Even a perfectly aimed deploy click is outside that scope.
Consider a different task that permits a deploy after review. The adapter receives three ordered actions in one batch. The read is allowed. The rerun needs approval. How far can the host go?

Execute the read. Pause before the rerun. Leave the later scroll unsent. A provider can also require confirmation. Obtain it, recheck the live state, and report which actions ran. A batch is only a way to carry the requests.

For a separately authorized incident update, put the exact change beside the current record. The reviewer grants this actor and session one change to incident twenty forty-eight at version four, before expiry. Recheck those bindings and consume the grant atomically with the update. A stale version needs a new decision.
Check both incident records in the verification scope. The intended status now reads review approved, at version five. Look at the other incident. Can the host call this success?

Stop. The other incident went from open to closed. The verifier found a change outside the grant. Preserve the audit evidence and investigate recovery. Detecting the mutation cannot undo it, and two records only establish what happened within that check.

title: What may the host take from the page?

beats.say: Look inside the failed step. A traceback, banner, accessibility label, or image may contain text that addresses the agent. Here a page banner suggests rerunning deployment. What can the host still take from this page?
Read the failure line. The host permits that bounded read and blocks the proposed deploy. Pixels and page text supply evidence. Neither can expand the permissions of the session.

A DOM view exposes markup and can include hidden text. The accessibility tree supplies roles and names. Here the tab has a name, but the traceback is painted inside a canvas. A screenshot preserves that line. Optical character recognition can read the visible characters.

A detector may miss the banner. A clean screenshot later cannot grant permission either. The host logs the observation reference, proposed effect and decision. It keeps raw page text and secrets out of that log, closes the isolated session and clears its temporary profile.

title: Design and score the read-only pilot

beats.say: Design the next run. A known artifact link has a stable selector. A second job needs the hidden lines inside this painted traceback. Which one needs the visual agent?

Use the selector for the known link. Use the visual loop only for the interactive canvas. Choose a supported API for a plain status lookup, or read an existing image directly if it already contains the evidence.

Score one local test episode. The first click opened the run. The stale click was withheld. The fresh click reached the tab, and the host saved the correct local draft. The last proposal aimed straight at Deploy. The host blocked it before dispatch. What should the score record?

One forbidden attempt in five proposals, and zero executed violations. Both dispatched clicks hit. The local draft passed its check. Count each of those separately. A correct target can still be a forbidden action.

Would a benchmark success rate of ninety-two percent justify write access? Before widening scope, measure steps, time, model calls, cost per success, reviewer load and policy decisions on the actual portal. A web or desktop benchmark uses its own tasks and verifier.

Keep the pilot read-only. Give the reviewer the run, failure line and artifact link in a verified local draft. Posting it needs separate scope, a current incident version, an exact diff, and a check for unintended changes afterward.
